metadata.title: Das politische Mindset von 14‐Jährigen: Ergebnisse der International Civic and Citizenship Education Study 2016

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The report uses ICCS 2016 student data for the target population of 8th-grade students in Nordrhein-Westfalen (NRW). The sampling design is a stratified multi-stage cluster sample with oversampling of Gymnasien with higher shares of students with migration background; the international study center provided student-level weights to adjust for differences between the intended and realized samples across selection strata. Weights were applied in the estimation of population parameters (e.g., weighted means) and the report also uses Jackknife repeated replication to estimate sampling errors, creating multiple Jackknife zones from paired schools within strata. The manuscript does not indicate that weights were omitted for the student analyses; instead, it explicitly states that weights and Jackknife are used via the IEA IDB Analyzer.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is an official IEA/OECD technical report or assessment framework. It describes sampling, scaling, and instrument design rather than student-level predictive modeling. Plausible values are therefore not applicable to the document's primary analytic purpose; any missing-data discussion refers to fieldwork or scaling procedures, not a single ML imputation strategy.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Analyses focus on ICCS 2016 students in NRW in grade 8 at general education schools. The sampling frame excludes Waldorfschulen and Förderschulen (curricular/teaching-method differences), and also applies additional exclusions at class/student level (e.g., classes consisting only of students unable to participate for physical/emotional/cognitive reasons; students speaking the test language for less than one year; removal of classes with low student participation on the student level). After dataset creation, further classes are removed when the participation rate at student level is below 50% to limit systematic nonresponse bias. For the reported student background-variable analyses, missing values in background variables are handled by listwise deletion (no imputation), meaning students without valid responses on the relevant background variables are excluded from those specific comparisons.

data.outcome_summary: This Waxmann report presents ICCS 2016 results for 8th-grade students in Nordrhein-Westfalen, focusing on political mindset dimensions. For political knowledge, the report uses Rasch-scaled achievement with five plausible values and compares weighted population estimates across countries and subgroups. NRW’s political knowledge mean is 519 (SE 2.7), close to the international mean (517) but below the European comparison group (535). The report documents substantial subgroup disparities: girls outperform boys by about 14 scale points in NRW; students with migration background score about 35 points lower; and books at home show a very large gap (more than 25 books vs ≤25 books: Δ=-76). Methodologically, the study is not an ML predictive modeling paper (no ML algorithms or ML performance metrics are reported), and missing background-variable data are handled via listwise deletion.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a descriptive large-scale assessment report (ICCS 2016) rather than an empirical machine-learning study. The manuscript reports scale construction (Rasch), plausible values, and weighted comparisons across countries and subgroups, but it does not train or evaluate any ML predictive models; therefore ml_techniques.primary is null and all_techniques is empty. As a result, there are no ML model performance metrics (e.g., accuracy/AUC/RMSE) to extract, and the extraction focuses on ICCS scale-based outcomes and subgroup differences.
